newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch now see 1996 EMU deficit of 1.9 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Dutch now see 1996 EMU deficit of 1.9 pct of GDP.

text.p: The Netherlands has further lowered its estimate of the 1996 Dutch EMU public sector deficit to 1.9 percent from 2.1 percent, a Finance Ministry spokeswoman said on Friday.
Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm had mentioned the new estimate to members of parliament on Thursday, she said, adding that it remained a provisional figure.
In January the Finance Ministry reported that the estimated 1996 EMU deficit had been revised down to 2.1 percent of GDP from a 2.6 percent estimate published in September.
It said then that the 1996 EMU public sector debt estimate had been lowered to 78.5 percent of GDP from 78.8 percent in September. Zalm did not mention a new EMU debt estimate.
The Maastricht treaty stipulates that to qualify for EMU, a country's deficit should be below three percent of GDP and its debt below 60 percent of GDP or declining towards that level.
